{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Transit agencies must continue to provide paratransit services for seniors, dialysis patients, and people with disabilities.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Discontinuation of paratransit service because of fiscal challenges during the pandemic would cut vulnerable people off from basic mobility.",
"claim_types":["prediction"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Paratransit services cost about 10 times as much per passenger mile as fixed-route transit.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Paratransit services comprise about 9 percent of transit agencies’ budget.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Transit agencies need additional federal funding to be able to continue vitally needed paratransit service as they face added financial strain because of the coronavirus crisis.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Transit workers must be considered essential workers, on par with utility, sanitation, and grocery workers, since transit operations need to continue during the pandemic.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"As essential workers, transit workers must have access to personal protective equipment (PPE) for the duration of the pandemic.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Providing appropriate PPE to approximately 375,000 transit vehicle operators and vehicle and facility maintenance workers nationwide for a duration of 6 months is essential, which may be a conservative estimate of the duration of the pandemic.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
